title: National evidence reconciliation matrix — Observatory #39 vs #42

summary.note: Full per-record rows generated offline during reconciliation; decision document is authoritative. Shared official core and both Lagos IGR figures are retained.

lagosIgrDiscrepancy.description: Lagos State 2025 IGR reported differently by two secondary sources

budgit.publisher: BudgIT Foundation · 2026 State of States Report

lagosIgrDiscrepancy.decision: Retain both records with explicit mutual reference in limitations. Do not average, prefer, or suppress either figure.

rationale: Shared official core (WHO, NIMC, NPHCDA, IMF, NITDA) is identical and should form the verified foundation.
#39 contributes the state-budget source-coverage register (37 jurisdictions) — valuable as a readiness catalogue, not as extracted data.
#39 contributes Agora 2025 aggregates and selected state BIR-derived figures with clear secondary status.
#42 contributes denser BudgIT H1-2026 health actual-spend by state; these are secondary and should be included only with their published limitations.
A pure choice of either #39 or #42 would discard material high-quality secondary coverage from the other branch.
A new consolidated branch starting from main, importing the shared official set + carefully attributed secondary sets + the coverage register, produces one auditable national evidence dataset.
preferFrom39: Selected state-level BIR figures (Anambra Q3 2026, etc.) with secondary status
Lagos IGR (Agora) kept alongside BudgIT figure
preferFrom42: BudgIT H1-2026 health actual-spend by state (with internal aggregate discrepancy noted)
Other unique published_research records that carry explicit limitations
excludeOrDefer: Any record lacking sourceUrl and clear publisher
Any record that converts national figures into state/LGA without supporting data (none detected in these two branches)
Records whose primary documents remain inaccessible and whose secondary report does not state methodology
